scratchInvariant: The only product edit changes the PC fused launch constant and its platform guard/comment. No resource declaration, size calculation, binding, descriptor, or allocation changes. Huffman tables remain ephemeral in the existing 6456-byte group-local LDS allocation; neither a persistent table nor an equivalent global buffer is introduced. Prefix buffers retain their existing per-table capacity; only their computed group counts change from ceil(N/32) to ceil(N/64). Therefore the base's full 1076-byte global scratch reduction per compressed block is preserved.
hypothesis: A 64-thread fused Huffman group may recover part of the RX 6900 XT throughput loss by distributing group-local table construction across twice as many threads and allowing up to 64 streams to share that construction.
mechanism: Change only the existing shared PC literal-group constant from 32 to 64. The host prefix pass already consumes that constant; HLSL numthreads and the fused entry-point tgSize argument consume it too. Table construction and scalar DWORD-store decoding already distribute work using tgSize. No decoder, table-generation algorithm, output cache, resource allocation, shader permutation, or wave-size attribute changes.

expected.status: Unbuilt and unmeasured proposal; no asserted performance headroom or win.
expected.metric: Exact CI geometric mean of GB/s at rungs 64,128,192,256,384,512,768,1024; five sweeps per rung using the unchanged perf_manifest corpus and pooling.
expected.benefit: Per-thread table-expansion iterations change from ceil(statePairCount/32) to ceil(statePairCount/64). Tables shared by more than 32 streams need ceil(N/64) regenerations rather than ceil(N/32). This is static work distribution, not a claim that elapsed table-build time halves.
expected.limitation: Tables serving only one or four streams still require exactly one regeneration. Such cases receive only the table-build parallelism change, while their decode lane utilization decreases.

wiredSurfaces: zstdgpu.cpp:2767-2771 supplies kzstdgpu_TgSizeX_DecompressLiterals to the host prefix binding.
Shaders\ZstdGpuComputePrefixSum.hlsl:59-69 computes ceil(streamCount/literalsPerGroup), per-table inclusive group ends, and total DecompressLiteralsGroups.
Shaders\ZstdGpuUpdateDispatchArgs.hlsl:100 emits that group count into the existing DecompressLiterals dispatch slot.
Shaders\ZstdGpuInitHuffmanTableAndDecompressLiterals.hlsl:35,42-45 uses the same constant for numthreads and tgSize and rejects surplus dispatch groups uniformly.
zstdgpu_shaders.h:2825-2918 passes tgSize through table pre-initialization, table expansion, and literal decoding.
zstdgpu_shaders.h:2949-2954 uses tgSize both for per-table stream offset and the partial-group bound.
unchanged: Full 1076-byte per-compressed-block global scratch reduction; no restored or equivalent global Huffman table buffer.
Huffman Get/Consume protocol, table-generation implementation, scalar DWORD head/interior/tail output semantics, and all resource/SRT layouts.
Existing Xbox One 64-thread geometry and Scarlett/generic Xbox 32-thread geometry.
Unrelated FSE and sequence kernel launch constants; the only additional occurrence of this literal constant in InitFseTable is an existing comment, not executable code.
CPU emulation continues to recompute prefixes for one stream per group and passes tgSize=1.
scope.vendorRouting: The fused Huffman kernel is a shared runtime kernel, not a vendor-specialized permutation. Consequently this experiment changes every PC vendor. Adding AMD-only shader routing would require extra compiled variants/build changes beyond this surgical candidate; no such routing is introduced.

correctnessArgument.validation: Read-only source tracing and reasoned bounds/mapping review only. No builds, compilation, tests, measurement, RDP, package operations, or subagents were used. git diff --check was clean.
correctnessArgument.groupPartition: For a table with N streams, the prefix allocates G=ceil(N/64) groups. Local group j in [0,G) owns offsets 64*j through min(64*j+63,N-1). Every stream offset s has unique j=floor(s/64) and thread s mod 64. Since j<G implies 64*j<N, N-64*j cannot underflow for a dispatched nonempty table group.
correctnessArgument.oneAndFourStreams: N=1 activates only thread 0 for decode; N=4 activates threads 0..3. All 64 threads complete the unchanged group-uniform table construction and barriers before the bounded decode loop. Inactive decode threads do not load LitRefs or write outputs.
correctnessArgument.multipleGroupsAndPartialTails: N=64 has one full group; N=65 has one full group and a tail with only thread 0; N=128 has two full groups. In general remain=min(N-64*j,64) excludes inactive tail threads. Stream ranges have neither gaps nor overlap.
correctnessArgument.treeless: HufLitIdToLitStreamId is recorded only for full-tree literal blocks. Each table's range still ends at the next full-tree stream start, or HUF_Streams for the last table; intervening treeless blocks therefore retain their inherited table. Only the partition of that unchanged stream range into groups changes.
correctnessArgument.unusedTableSlotsAndPaddedDispatch: Unused table slots contribute zero groups to the existing prefix; binary-search table lookup is unchanged. The existing group-uniform check against DecompressLiteralsGroups rejects padded indirect groups before any group barrier.
correctnessArgument.tableBuild: All FOR_WORK_ITEMS loops now enumerate threadId+64*k rather than threadId+32*k; the 64 residue classes cover each existing bounded work-item range once. LDS allocation and indices are unchanged. Maximum 11-bit tables have 1024 packed state pairs: 16 expansion iterations per thread rather than 32, with identical destinations and values.
correctnessArgument.wavesAndSynchronization: PreInit already derives laneCnt=min(threadCnt,WaveGetLaneCount()), waveCnt=threadCnt/laneCnt, and waveOfs from wave index. For wave32, two waves write the alternating 32-bit ballot words; for wave64, one wave writes both ballot halves. With at most 256 weights, both cover exactly the existing eight ballot words per digit. Smaller waves retain the existing zero-initialize/atomic-OR path, while wider waves use laneCnt=64 and the first two ballot words. GroupMemoryBarrierWithGroupSync remains group-wide at every LDS handoff, including the final expansion-to-decode handoff.
correctnessArgument.output: Each stream retains exactly one decoding owner. Its input segment, output segment, Get/Consume order, and aligned DWORD/byte stores are unchanged, so increasing group membership introduces no new inter-stream write ownership.

risks: All-PC portability impact: NVIDIA, Intel, and other AMD architectures may regress. RX 6900 XT success would not establish a cross-vendor win; promotion requires independent validation or a later vendor-specific routing change.
Wave size remains driver-selected. TG64 may use two wave32s or one wave64; it does not force wave64 or guarantee full-wave occupancy.
Two wave32s per group can increase cross-wave barrier overhead and allocated register footprint relative to TG32; table-build work redistribution may not compensate.
For one-/four-stream tables the second wave32 has no decode work, yet its group may retain resources until the active wave finishes.
Larger stream groups can worsen divergent long-tail retention or reduce independently schedulable groups, especially when streams sharing a table have uneven lengths.
The source mapping proof does not replace the evaluator's compilation, GPU correctness, and paired-control performance gates.
nextIdea: Only if evaluator profiling shows TG64 loses mainly to wave32 tail occupancy, consider a separate experiment retaining 64 cooperative build threads while decoupling a smaller stream-group stride. Do not stack it onto this proposal without measuring this candidate first.
